title: Notes - my most used app
body:
Update: For some reason, when I am entering data (typing or voice to text), it will sometimes jump to another place in the note, often to the bottom (annoying in a long note).  Double tapping to paste info where there is no other text, often results in highlighting a word in a nearby paragraph.  It gets a little frustrating.  

(1) Editing with voice-to-text: With voice-to-text turned on, tapping a word to highlight it often causes the page to scroll to the bottom.  In long notes, that’s a problem.
(2) Stop with all the added commas, please.  I don’t want extra commas randomly thrown into my sentences or phrases.  They often change the meaning and make it difficult to understand.  It takes more time to delete the added punctuation, than it did to say it in the first place.
(3) ‘Notes’ is my most used app.  As frustrating as the little details are, I don’t know what I would do without it.  So thank you!😃

title: Great for Inter-Device Note Sharing
body: I use Notes to keep one set of shopping lists that I can access from any device. Sometimes Notes gets confused, however, and is slow to keep a list synced and up to date with the latest version. Like many apps, it has reached functional saturation, meaning that in some situations or on some screens it becomes difficult to type, or too easy to press the wrong buttons and lose data. I also use it to share scripts to my mobile teleprompter for online content creation, which requires tiresome mental gymnastics to keep everything coordinated, but that’s an interoperability issue that no one app can control. The fact that I’ve ended up using the native Notes app instead of other, often more specialized apps attests to the ephemeral nature of non-native apps over time. One day the developer decides they’ve lost their competitive edge, folds up shop and stops maintaining the app, which collectively drives everyone back to Apple’s native apps, which have the built-in longevity characteristic of a company that is not likely to just fold up overnight.

title: Here’s a sincere English comment hoping for LaTeX support in the software
body:
Dear Developers,

First of all, thank you for creating such a helpful and user-friendly software! It has truly made my daily tasks much more efficient. However, as a student/researcher/educator (feel free to specify), I often need to write mathematical formulas, equations, or scientific notations in my work. Currently, the lack of LaTeX support makes it challenging to present complex content neatly and professionally.

LaTeX is an essential tool for anyone working with academia, STEM fields, or technical writing. Enabling LaTeX support would not only enhance the software’s functionality but also make it a go-to choice for a wider community of users. Imagine how seamlessly we could draft academic notes, solve problem sets, or prepare teaching materials with beautiful typeset equations!

I understand that implementing this might require time and effort, but it would mean a great deal to those of us who rely on precise mathematical formatting. Your consideration of this feature would be extremely grateful, and I’m confident it would take the software to an even higher level of excellence.

Thank you for always listening to user feedback!

Warm regards

title: Feature Suggestion: Center Alignment Option for Apple Notes
body:
As a long-time user of the Apple Notes app, I truly appreciate its functionality and how seamlessly it allows me to organize my thoughts. One feature I believe would enhance the user experience is the ability to center text within a note. Currently, achieving a centered layout requires manually pressing the space bar multiple times, which is not ideal for formatting or visual balance.

I respectfully suggest adding a simple “center alignment” option to the formatting toolbar. While it may seem like a minor tweak, this addition would provide users with greater creative control and elevate the app’s versatility. Thank you for considering this improvement—small changes can make a big impact.

Sincerely,
An Apple client since Gen 1 iPhone (2007). Still here. Still loyal. Still evolving. 😎

title: Blue lines
body:
Make it so you can turn off the blue lines under handwriting.  It’s so annoying and also feels like a mind bogglingly obvious thing to include.   

Who made the conscious decision “Most people that are taking notes by hand probably want blue lines to appear under everything they write with no way to turn it off!”  


——

Months later. Still weird blue lines under everything you write by hand. 

It’s actually amazing how lame it is. Like obviously the people who make this never write by hand on their iPad, or if they do they do not use this app. 

Imagine writing on paper in class, taking notes, and someone is standing next to you with a blue highlighter and they highlight all the words they can’t read. 

You can read them just fine, and you aren’t writing it for someone else to read, but it doesn’t matter. They just keep highlighting everything. And they won’t stop. No matter what you do. 

This app gives you that experience.

title: Apple Notes Drains Battery
body:
1)URLs seem to be part of the problem.  30 to 50 percent of my battery life was being used for notes.  I found a few old notes with dead (404 not found) url links and evidence these were continually trying to access the expired pages. Why are they trying to access any pages if not pressed and also if the app is not open?
When I deleted the dead links, battery life improved considerably, however, there may be additional issues causing the battery drain, I don’t know why links would need to access the Internet if the particular note isn’t in use and if the link has not been clicked upon.
Also, since the recent update, it has been performing more slowly.
If I replace a url by pasting over it, it pastes a format over the old url instead of replacing the url.
2) Notes will often abruptly end to the home screen when I delete a column in a table.  This is not a new problem but it is very annoying!
3) Notes Folders do not consistently sort alphabetically.  This problem has been reported for at least three years with no work around or resolution!!!!!!

title: Severely Outdated and Lacking Intelligence
body:
Apple Notes feels like a relic—non-intuitive, overly basic, and stuck in the past. Despite the power of the iPhone 16 Pro Max, this app lacks modern design cues, meaningful customization, or real integration. The default yellow-paper aesthetic looks completely out of place on a flagship device.

Smart features consistently underdeliver. Where’s the AI integration with Siri? Why can’t I set alarms, build intelligent schedules, or receive contextual suggestions? Customization is nonexistent. Syncing is functional but uninspired.

This isn’t a productivity tool—it’s a fallback.

Basic features if you’re basic. Doesn’t wow me.

One last thing—why are so many negative reviews still rated five stars? If users are “devastated,” the score should match. Just saying.

title: Inability to sort FOLDERS alphabetically undercuts this app
body:
The iOS Notes app has many nice features, but, the more you use this app, the more likely you are to have many folders, each containing many notes.  

The ordering of many folders over a long time is likely to be fractured into several alphabetical sequences embedded within and wrapped around one another. The user will find locating folders and notes unnecessarily tedious. 

This glaring oversight needs to be addressed, or else the Notes application will be passed over as a useless toy, failing the needs of anyone who needs to recover information quickly and efficiently.

title: Bad
body:
Why Notes is a Bad App

The Notes app, often pre-installed on smartphones, tablets, and computers, is one of the most commonly used tools for jotting down thoughts, reminders, ideas, and lists. While it may seem like an innocuous and convenient tool, there are several reasons why the Notes app is inadequate for a variety of users, especially those who rely heavily on digital tools for organization, collaboration, and productivity. Despite its widespread use, the Notes app suffers from limitations that hinder its effectiveness as a primary organizational and note-taking solution. This essay will explore the shortcomings of the Notes app in terms of its functionality, lack of advanced features, security concerns, poor collaboration tools, and failure to integrate with other productivity tools.

1. Limited Features

One of the most significant drawbacks of the Notes app is its limited set of features. At its core, the app allows users to create simple text notes. However, when compared to other more robust note-taking apps, the Notes app feels primitive and underwhelming. Many other note-taking apps, such as Evernote, OneNote, or Notion, provide advanced features like formatting options, hierarchical note organization, customizable templates, and the ability to add rich media such as images, videos, and voice memos.

The Notes app, on the other hand, offers a fairly basic text editor that lacks many of these features. For example, it does not support rich text formatting in a way that allows users to easily highlight, bold, or underline text. While it does allow some basic formatting like lists, headings, and checkboxes, the app falls short in providing a fully customizable and intuitive writing experience. This lack of versatility makes it difficult for users to create structured and visually appealing notes, especially for more complex information.

Furthermore, the app’s simple structure means that users can’t easily organize their notes into categories or notebooks. Instead, they are stuck with a basic list of notes, making it difficult to manage large amounts of information. In comparison to alternatives like Evernote, which provides multi-level notebooks and tagging systems, the Notes app’s organizational abilities are inadequate.

2. Lack of Cross-Platform Compatibility

Another significant issue with the Notes app is its lack of seamless cross-platform compatibility. While the app is available on Apple devices, including iPhones, iPads, and Macs, it is not available on Android or Windows platforms. This can be a major inconvenience for users who use multiple devices across different operating systems. As a result, if a user needs to access their notes on a non-Apple device, they are forced to look for third-party apps or use workarounds, such as emailing themselves the notes or using cloud storage solutions.

In contrast, other note-taking apps like Google Keep and Evernote are designed with cross-platform functionality in mind. These apps are available on both Apple and Android devices and can sync notes seamlessly across different platforms. This ensures that users can access their notes anywhere, regardless of the device they are using, and eliminates the friction caused by the lack of cross-platform support that the Notes app suffers from.

3. Security Concerns

Security is another area where the Notes app falls short. While the app does offer password protection for individual notes and the ability to lock notes with Face ID or Touch ID, it is not as secure as other alternatives. The password protection system is relatively simple and does not provide advanced encryption options for sensitive data. Users looking for a higher level of security for their notes may find the Notes app inadequate in safeguarding their private information.

Moreover, when it comes to cloud storage, the Notes app relies on iCloud to sync and back up data. While iCloud is generally secure, it is not immune to security breaches or hacking attempts. Users who store highly sensitive information on the Notes app may feel uncomfortable relying solely on iCloud, especially considering that iCloud accounts have been the target of data breaches in the past.

In comparison, other note-taking apps like Evernote or Microsoft OneNote offer more robust security measures, including the ability to encrypt individual notes or notebooks and more granular control over who has access to shared content. These apps also allow users to back up their notes to third-party cloud storage solutions, offering greater flexibility and control over the security of their data.

4. Poor Collaboration Tools

Another significant flaw in the Notes app is its limited ability to support collaboration. While it does allow users to share notes with others via iCloud, the collaboration features are rudimentary at best. Users cannot easily work on the same note simultaneously, and there is no support for version history, which means that once a note is edited, the previous versions are lost. This makes the app unsuitable for teams or individuals who need to collaborate in real-time on shared notes or documents.

In comparison, apps like Google Docs and Microsoft OneNote offer much more advanced collaboration features. Google Docs, for example, allows users to collaborate in real-time on the same document, with each user’s changes visible instantly. Additionally, both Google Docs and OneNote offer comprehensive version history, allowing users to revert to previous versions of a note or document. These features make collaboration much easier and more efficient, especially for users who need to share information and work together on projects.

5. Inadequate Search Functionality

title: Long-term survival.
body:
I tried a lot of note keeping programs, but none of them were really suitable for the long-term. I’m being realistic about cross platform enter operability. I have used DOS, Windows, Macintosh, and Linux for decades and Macs, and associated hardware, since the middle of 84. My favorite program of all time may be HyperCard out of which sprang programs like the Myst universe, and a simple way for an independent to be able to build a business for somebody who has a hankering for coding, playing with electronics, and making Super 8 movies with his friends. We each had talents, but we learned from each other a circle of three. 

Reminders is a familiar bookshelf, I can have shopping lists, to do lists, or lists of any kind. Timed reminders that are reflected very quickly in every device that I have. That keeps my body functioning. 

But Notes, is a tool of mind that I can use to collect my thoughts and train an AI on my miscellaneous writings.

title: Help
body:
I love using the Notes app for its convenient document scanning feature, but I feel like it could benefit from a few important updates. While scanning documents within the app is straightforward, the functionality is currently limited in terms of what can be done with the scanned files.

It would be incredibly helpful if Apple could add the following features:
1. **Enhanced File Saving Options:** The ability to save scanned documents as different file formats such as Word documents (.docx) or PDFs directly within the app.
2. **Seamless Sharing:** An integrated option to send scanned documents via email, fax, or other sharing platforms without needing to use external apps.
3. **Improved Organization:** Features to easily organize and categorize scanned documents within folders or by tags.

Additionally, it would be helpful if I didn't have to go outside Apple and pay extra for these features from a third party. Adding these capabilities would streamline workflow, making the Notes app an even more powerful tool for both personal and professional use. I look forward to seeing these updates in future versions!

Thank you, Apple, for considering this feedback!

title: Notes self-delete at random
body:
I have always had my Notes backed up to iCloud, but I've gone back to search for certain Notes I've created and saved — ones I was CERTAIN I had saved. Quite a few of them I had saved in the presence of another person who could confirm that I had done it (such as shopping lists, ideas for songs, etc.) Later, I would search for them but find them gone from my phone and my iCloud backup as if they had never existed, yet other notes saved on the same day would still be there. 

I now text reminders to myself instead of using Notes because my texts are always backed up. I see and hear many other iOS users complaining of saved Notes going missing, so I know it isn't just me this is happening to.

I'm a teacher, so I know that high school and college students who can't afford a laptop will write their papers on their phones using Notes. I hate to think of how many missing assignments this random deletion has caused. 

It would be nice if this could be fixed.

title: A remnant from the Sculley Dark Ages
body:
Tom’s Hardware Premium Review!
Apple’s hastily assembled text entry app was doomed to failure from the start. Apple’s “Notes,” reportedly assembled in one day by a member of the Apple HQ airport driving team, consistently ranks as the worst and most useless app. Ever. How it  somehow managed to squeeze the world’s most boring tile game included with Classic Mac, OS7, to second place is a mystery (though it shouldn’t be).

This most negligent failure of an app is oddly upgraded without concern for its underlying failure to function. 

Samsung is wise to continue to compare Apple’s failure to thrive iOS and the Notes programming nightmare to their own 21st century Android note taking system that easily scales to enterprise level note taking and data parsing capabilities, while Apple’s Notes fails to load.

Apple’s iOS notes seems to have been deliberately designed to fail courtesy of bloated CPU/RAM intensive code that makes Microsoft Word seem remarkably portable.

Apple’s Notes have done an extraordinary job in helping Samsung motivate folks to switch from Apple’s tired and unremarkable iOS, a boring continually patched mobile operating system that hasn’t at all changed since 2007. Advertisements shouting out “Apple Intelligence” as if it were at all functional and anything anyone asked for, immediately falls flat when Apple’s own iOS apps, i.e., Notes, haven’t changed in nearly 20 years.

title: Good app, serious flaw…
body: I really like using this app precisely because it is simple and that is the way it should be for notes. I just recently got an iPad with the Apple Pencil, and it is a fantastic combination, but the Apple Notes app was completely not up to the task. In my use for handwriting, which I do a lot of for working with problems and ideas, I found it draining my battery life disproportionately. After 20 minutes of journaling it took 10% of my battery with it! I charged my iPad to full, hooked it up to charger with a watt meter, and measured the power draw. The ipad at the medium brightness is hovering around 1.5 watts, when writing its hanging around 7-9 watts, and peaking at 11 watts! I switched to good notes for handwriting, and using the same brightness, still fully charged, and plugged in to that watt meter, it was hovering around 2 watts, much better. I went to the internet to see if others have this issue, and it is a well documented issue. I do not understand how apple can have this kind of an issue on the Notes app. It is supremely disappointing and I hope they fix it. Until then I will go ahead and do the one time purchase of Goodnotes 6 for my handwriting uses.

Do you ever have that random inspiration to turn your life around at 3 AM in the morning and need to write your game plan down?

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

Do you ever need to write down your all time record for the farthest in the future you've made it scrolling on the calendar app?

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

Notes is there for you.

One is that when I have a very long text open in Notes and minimize it to share data from another app, I return to Notes and it is nowhere near where I left it before.  I have to do a lot of scrolling to get back to where I was.  Flipping back and forth several times and this creates a lot of extra work.  
Any note should be where I left it when I return to it.  
Another is that when I copy something from Note or another app and then go to paste it elsewhere into Note, I cannot put my cursor on the beginning of a blank line until something has been manually entered elsewhere in the text.  
It has been this way for a while.  I wish they would fix these two issues and render an update. 
I wish there was an option to set it to only handle text.  When links appear where I don't want them to [like phone numbers for example], it creates issues.  
You really need to rethink your development strategies.

title: Formatting Issues When Copying from ChatGPT😒
body:
I’ve been a longtime user of iOS Notes, but one recurring issue has been incredibly frustrating. Every time I copy and paste formatted text from ChatGPT into Notes, the formatting changes. Weird spacing appears, and the structure becomes inconsistent with how it originally looked. This makes the pasted text visually unappealing and time-consuming to fix.

For those of us who use Notes to organize our thoughts or quickly save polished content, this creates unnecessary friction. I’m not looking for Notes to replicate every app’s formatting perfectly, but maintaining basic structure, spacing, and alignment—especially when moving between apps like ChatGPT—would save users so much time and effort.

Please consider improving the paste functionality to honor the original formatting as closely as possible. It would make Notes even more indispensable for users who rely on it daily. Thank you… for now (I switched to using google notes instead because it keeps the integrity of the formatting. ☺️)

title: If you Lost your Notes… READ
body:
So after the new terms & conditions agreement, the Notes app will default to Outlook or another account that you have setup. 

I thought all my notes were gone when I opened the app today. 

After some changes to my settings, I restored them.

Go to Settings — and search ‘Note’ 
The iPhone Note app should be at the top, click it.
Now go to ‘Accounts’ 
The default account used to be the iCloud account 
It was changed to another one.
Turn off ‘Notes’ for all other accounts OTHER THAN your iCloud account. 
Exit the settings. 
Open your Notes app.
Swipe down and your notes should begin to repopulate.

title: Personal experience thus far
body:
The Notes app provides the ability to create and manage your notes, from personal thoughts to important information that you can set as a reminder. 

You can store and send information to any recipient, from your family members or entrusted friends, to not only organize your information but also to help sort through it, so as to ensure that the information is not lost or stolen, and of course is available for use globally- download-able through most devices, from Samsungs, iPhones, etcetera.

What more can you ask for than your personal information be stored, protected and edited by whom you see fit without any restrictions. 

Highly recommend to anyone that likes to organize and communicate their thoughts/needs with their friends and family alike.

title: Love the simplicity
body:
I love the simplicity of Apple Notes and indeed all Apple products. 
I think an improvement that could be made to Notes though, is to add additional formatting and structuring options to Apple Notes. Having more than 1 Heading and 1subheading will give users the ability to customize and format their notes for readability. Also, the structuring of linking and back-linking Notes would be a powerful feature. This would essentially allow a user to have a Table of Contents that contains a link to all their notes, and with the back-link each individual page would be linked back to the table of contents.

title: Handwriting recognition killed this app
body:
Ever since the implementation of handwriting recognition, this app has been prone to overheating & crashing. It is unacceptable for this to occur on your flagship M4 PRO tablet that you market as a notetaking device. 

For the app to reliably crash and lose an hour of work makes it unreliable. I will not use it. I've gone back to pen and paper because of how foul this experience has become. 

It is a classic case of fixing something that was not broken. The notes app was my favorite application. A place to think freely like pen on paper. Now it's an unusable slog of autocorrect underlines. 

Apple had been a champion of user-centered experiences, with simple tools. Which brain dead bozo lost the plot and thought shipping an unusable, unstable, unreliable tool that broke the notes app on your flagship tablet was a good idea?

Ditch the handwriting recognition. Let me toggle it off. Quit your job. Whatever it takes to make your product actually work. 

Do better!

title: Too many issues
body: I pay for iCloud+ and I am full in the Apple ecosystem owning an iPhone 13 Pro Max, M1 iPad Pro, M1 Pro MacBook Pro 14”, and more hoping for a seamless and flawless experience. However, that has not been the case with the Apple Notes app which I rely heavily on in college to take handwritten notes with the Apple Pencil on PDFs. First, my biggest gripe is the iCloud Sync issues where hours of progress are not saved. Second, for some reason, when using the Apple Pencil, my M1 iPad Pro gets extremely hot and the battery life drains like crazy. Third, the app frequently crashes for no reason at all. You would think an app made by Apple would be better than this, but it is not. I have researched online and many other people have these frustrating issues with no solution to give. There are countless posts to Apple Support, but they do not help at all. I have even submitted several reports on the Feedback app as I have a developer account, but none of my concerns have been addressed. I understand that alternatives like Goodnotes and Notability exist, but I hold a strong opinion against subscription services unless they are absolutely necessary. Please Apple, fix these issues. I KNOW you know they exist. You have the most intelligent software engineers in the world so this should be a piece of cake to solve. Many loyal customers including myself have been getting increasingly frustrated. This is simply unacceptable from one of the largest tech companies on the planet.

title: Not Optimized for iPad
body:
I was so hopeful that iPad OS 18 would solve the chronic issues with Apple Notes, but unfortunately it does not.

This application is in many ways the focal point of the iPad - the Apple Pencil is part and parcel with Apple Notes, and nearly every advertisement you see with the iPad shows the Apple Pencil, Pencil 2, or Pencil Pro writing on Apple Notes.

Unfortunately, since iPad OS 16 or so, and specifically on M-Series processors, this application simply cannot run efficiently. After about 10 minutes of standard “note taking,” even at low brightness levels and while not charging, the application causes iPad’s to heat up to completely unreasonable temperatures, making the device uncomfortable to hold, putting unnecessary wear on the device, and wiping out the battery life. The problem is especially emphasized when using a longer note, or annotating a PDF.

I find it incredibly disappointing that in spite of all of the reviews and threads and calls to Apple Support, nothing is done about this. I find it outrageous to claim that the act of writing with a pencil on the screen, something which Samsung and Kindle devices can do with absolutely no trouble, causes an M4 processor (Apple’s most powerful custom processor) to exceed 40°C.

As far as I am concerned, the iPad is not a serious tool for business people or students as long as this application remains in its current condition. This should be THE app the iPad was made for, it comes standard on every device sold - and yet it is so challenging for the processor to run that it takes more of a toll than a AAA game. Incredible.

For whatever reason, turning on “Battery Saver” prevents the heat issue by throttling the CPU, so while the heat is gone, the pencil input becomes laggy and cumbersome.

There used to be workarounds like using Goodnotes or another alternative, however the new M2/M4 iPads seem to cause the input on these devices to lag. My only option for taking notes on a $1,000 device built for that specific purpose, is to deal with heat that makes it uncomfortable to hold.

And the worst part is, it’s a software issue, so every time it happens, I know they could fix it if they wanted to. But they won’t. And that’s frustrating.

title: Microsoft Word Mobile
body:
I love, LO-V-E, this app! I have been using it for years. Originally, as a kid, I used it to store some photos into with little captions. I even made a couple of visual novels and stored some childhood dreams in there… but as I grew older, I have learned about and been exposed to the business world. 
Now, as an adult, I use this app essentially as my daily business (and personal) tool for making: charts, bulletin boards, numbered lists, checklists, and text documents (with attachments and font customization).
This app is very user friendly, as there are small pictures of the inputs I’ve listed above; The user can also use keyboard shortcuts if they choose. 
To further elaborate on the font customization, you can choose between four font sizes: Title, Subtitle, Heading, and Normal, and you can choose from four five font types: Standard, Bold, Underline, Strikethrough, and Mono-style. Although the app doesn’t have different style fonts (like Times New Roman or Comic Sans), the user can simply copy/paste text onto a font generator site and it will likely register the font type.
To add to the user friendliness, organization with the app is flexible, as notes can be divided into folders; and subfolders can be added to folders. It can get a bit confusing when too many folders are opened at one time, so I always remember to close my folders once I’m done using them.
Overall, this app is user friendly with good customization with limited, but easily accessible features.

title: Would rate Zero if possible
body:
I use Notes on an outdated iPhone where I have less than good storage. I don’t have a phone number on this phone, so I don’t use it much outside of two or three games and Notes. As an aspiring author, I depended on notes a lot in writing my books. However, I wasn’t able to use anything else (Google Docs, Microsoft Word, other Notes App, etc.) because it notified me I didn’t have enough storage. “No,” I said. “That can’t be right, I don’t have enough apps to take up 17 Gbs of storage!”
I had four apps I used faithfully. Three of them added up to about four Gbs. The fourth was Notes. It took up THIRTEEN gigabytes of storage EMPTY!! 
Even worse, I lost 396 pages of progress on my book because it didn’t sync up. Worst app I’ve ever used. Will be deleting as soon as I can figure out how—which is another problem. 
Apple, please try to fix this. I need a reliable app for writing.

title: My Life Is Ruined: Killed My Dog And I’m On Probation
body:
August 25th, 2024, was the day I experienced one of the most tragic events in human history. I was sitting on my sofa watching the newest episode of Skibidi Toilet (Skibidi Toilet Episode 77 (part 1)) when I suddenly felt a trembling sensation in my stomach. Sprinting to the toilet, I tripped on my dog. Instantaneously, I heard all the bones in his body break. What’s worse: I didn’t even make it to the toilet. And to further worsen the day, I tripped onto my candle and caused my house to burn down. 16,000 acres of residential houses came down with it.

I documented this day in my Notes App, under the influence that this was a private and personal journal. Unfortunately, I assumed wrong. The Federal Bureau of Investigation had access to my Notes App. The sirens wailed outside my front door. 

“This is the FBI. Open the door!” I heard.

I was arrested for animal abuse and arson.

I now write this review under probation, with my trial happening on December 12th. Wish me luck 🫡. 

In conclusion, the Notes App has ruined my life and caused me immense stress. If you want your privacy, don’t expect the Notes App to fill that desire.

title: Love: Please Update Duplicate
body:
I love this app, use it everyday. 
However, for the last few weeks/months when I go to move an item on my list (usually to give it a higher priority) a “+” appears and it creates a duplicate line. I move the item then need to search back on the list to find the “original” and manually delete it.😭

This is new. The concept is good but moving the line item is the primary task. I can’t think of an occasion when I wanted to duplicate a task, therefore I would not use or need this feature.

I’ve tried everything to not duplicate. I can, once in a while, but there doesn’t seem to be a constant way. Maybe the duplicate could be off until the user turns it on?

I’ll keep using the app for now, going back and deleting lines I’m not choosing to duplicate with the hopes this is fixed. I searched Google and discovered I’m not the only one this is happening to. Please removed the auto duplicate or create a way to have absolute control over it.

Thank you!

title: Deletion
body: While this is a good app for simple note taking, it has a serious issue with a feature. When collaborating on a note there is a history section that shows when which text was written who wrote it, similar to google docs'. Unlike google docs, once text is deleted, even if by a different user that the one who wrote it, its history also gets deleted from the history section. This way, anyone in a shared note can delete others' work with no way of restoring a previous version or even finding out who did it. I don't know why they even bothered with a history section if it doesn't even show past versions. Months of my work have been erased - just use google docs

title: OMG everyone needs it
body:
tl;dr it's a great app that i use frequently and would highly recommend using.
So this might be my favorite app actually, as a songwriter (i haven't produced anything, i just...write lyrics), it's great to write songs and put them in albums and i LOVE the "lock note" feature because i occasionally make notes/songs about sensitive things. i like how everything is set up, it's extremely user-friendly, easy to navigate, and is not overwhelming or difficult to use! never had any bugs or anything, it's reliable, feels like a safe space to me tbh! i also like how you can put pics in a note and i REALLY appreciate that you can make it a smaller size! in my experience it hasnt been laggy if you have a lot of data in one note, but i also dont have many notes like that. you dont need wifi or data or anything so that's another bonus. i love how you can change things like italics, bold, underline, strikethrough, and style (title, subtitle, normal text etc, as well as monostyle), and that's all great! you can also make bullet lists that you can tap and then it'll put a check mark on it. i dont use that feature a ton but i think it's cool! i also like how you can draw in it, and how it has multiple drawing tools for that, im genuinely impressed by this idk!!! i wouldn't recommend Notes to be your go-to sketchbook app, but it's so cool aaaaa
Something i would change is, when you click on Aa to get to formatting/styling choices etc, i would add a selection of fonts you could pick from, so you could type in different fonts. not as many as Google Docs or anything, just a touch of variety in fonts would be GREATLY APPRECIATED❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️ If you read my entire rant about the Notes app, lol, i think you have too much time, but thanks anyway. Seriously though about the fonts...... But omggggg i love it so much!!!!! thank you for such a fabulous, useful app!!!❤️❤️❤️ ~cory :)

title: Why can’t we lock notes with attachments?
body:
I have been using the Apple Notes app for a while now, and overall, it’s a fantastic tool for organizing thoughts, ideas, and important information. The seamless integration with other Apple devices and services is particularly commendable. However, there is one glaring issue that significantly impacts the utility of the app: the inability to lock notes that contain attachments.

Security is a crucial aspect of note-taking apps, and while Apple Notes does offer the ability to lock notes, this feature becomes practically useless when it excludes notes with attachments. Attachments such as images, PDFs, and other documents often contain sensitive information that needs to be protected. The current limitation forces users to separate their attachments from the text, thereby disrupting the organization and coherence of the notes.

Why can’t we lock notes with attachments? This seems like a basic feature that should be included, especially given Apple’s emphasis on privacy and security. It’s frustrating to see that such an essential functionality is missing. I hope the developers address this issue soon, as it would greatly enhance the overall user experience and security of the app.

Until this feature is implemented, users seeking to keep their notes with attachments secure will have to look for alternative solutions. Please consider prioritizing this update to meet the security needs of your users.

title: Grid Issues - Useless
body:
1. Creating a grid requires you to enter text first 
2. You can only manually add one row or column at a time

5. Grid continues to lock up. Cells will become completely unusable and lack any ability to edit. Like the app doesn’t recognize they exist. The bug doesn’t resolve - it becomes embedded into the file so restarting doesn’t work. The information contained in those feels becomes effectively useless and inaccessible. At this stage, the grid itself is no longer able to be copied for information. Copying anything to paste into anew note copies it with a deep embedded bug that locks up multiple parts of the document, moves data around and changes actual inputs.

The only additional feature I would like is the option to show/hide the page break locations (would have to choose the intended paper size). Just a thin grey line or something. title: Needs dev features to be perfect
body:
My needs are not done well in industry unfortunately. Apple notes is close when you consider it comes with your Apple device purchase.
I need:
✅Typed notes
✅Tagging + smart searching or smart folders
✅handwritten notes (Apple Pencil)
✅pdf view and edit
✅offline access
✅Export to pdf or markdown

⭕️Structured diagramming tools with:
	connected lines that move with blocks or objects
	objects to move around
	object layer control (move to back)
⭕️Syntax highlighted code/cli blocks
⭕️vim motions while editing text
⭕️common syntax or shortcut for formatting (markdown preferred)

So basically obsidian combined with the os integrations of Apple notes and whiteboard of Freeform/miro.

Asking a lot, I know, but if Freeform got better stability and better offline mode and Apple notes got the vim motions, formatting of markdown syntax support, and syntax highlighted code blocks... Freeform + Apple notes would be industry leading... especially if their cross app linking went deeper than it currently can.

title: A few bits of frustrating UX
body:
Notes is in general really great, but there are a couple things that frustrate me:

I use an iPhone and a mac, and I put all my notes on iCloud so I can have them shared between devices. But they often get out of sync, which is fine but there is no way to manually refresh either to look for new changes. All I want is to be able to drag down and see a reloading symbol like on Safari or Mail. It annoys me to no end, and eventually I will have to switch to OneNote or something.

The other thing which is probably unreasonable to fix, but I might as well mention, are occasional lag spikes while typing. I’ll be typing a word and then my keyboard will stall for a few seconds and then it’ll glitch and make the text appear really fast. Not ideal, but I don’t know what optimization are possible here.

title: AVOID AT ALL COSTS
body: Eight hours of work down the drain, thanks Apple! Because of the ‘advanced’ automated save technology, a single Notes app crash derailed an entire day’s project. I did everything right: pausing for a 5-10 minute break when the iPad would get warm, regularly opening the note on my computer to ensure that it saved, and using the app on a new iPad with the most updated iOS. Even after two hours with customer support, it is unlikely that I can get my work back. Apple has major issues to fix with this app. From what I can tell based off a quick Google search and how the customer service advisors were speaking, this is a relatively frequent issue. You would think Apple wants to fix this issues, maybe by implementing a manual save option or version history to avoid errors of this type. This is not the first time I have experienced the issue, although normally no more than 20 minutes of work gets deleted. I would not have spent so long with customer support or hunting answers online if there wasn’t such a serious chunk of notes missing, and I’m sure the same is true for others who have posted online and called Apple for their note mysteriously vanishing. Apple, I’m begging that you fix this issue. This is really, really disheartening, and I only purchased an iPad to take notes. Given how popular of a feature note-taking is with iPads, one would think Apple puts time into investigating issues of this type. TLDR: Don’t use, pay for Goodnotes or notability. And a HUGE thanks (not) to Apple for knowingly producing an app with such major glitches yet no warnings or tips to avoid all of your notes going missing.

title: Would give zero stars if I could
body:
This app is incredibly basic and doesn’t allow for much customization with your notes, however I had overlooked that for a long time rather than just finding a new notes app to test out.
The other day I opened my notes app and all my notes were gone, no deleted folder to even check if they were in there, and despite supposedly being synced to my iCloud, I cannot recover them that way either. I, as well as many others according to reviews, relied on the notes app a lot for keeping critical work, health and personal information sorted and accessible whenever needed and now I don’t think I will ever get them back. My notes ranged from information about prescriptions for myself and my kids and what reactions we’ve had to them or what their efficacy was like, budgets, documentation of an ongoing work harassment issue, etc and now I’m out all that information for seemingly no reason and with no solution.
This seems to be common as of late considering how many reviewers have reported the same issue with no update on the possibility of getting their notes back. Not sure what happened or how Apple plans to fix this. Use another app if you rely on digital notes for any vital information. I’ve seen others recommend Evernote & One Note and I’ll be trying both of those instead.

- **Table of Contents**: A table of contents feature for longer notes would significantly improve navigation and accessibility, making the management of extensive information much more efficient.

title: I love this app.
body:
I would give 5 stars. But I believe the drawing aspect of this app could be improved.I vigorously use my iPad and my Apple Pencil and this app to draw diagrams and blueprints for my job in construction. The only thing I wish there was more of, is Shape configuration. (The ability to mirror, translate and rotate an already drawn shape or copy of one.) also the ability to save not so common shapes to some sort of memory bank for repetitions, or to allow for the “snap-to-shape” feature to just straighten the lines you’ve already drawn. (Currently you can only “snap-to-shape” basic shapes and angles.) Other than that I love this app and will continue to use it. I’ve figured ways around my above problems, but would love to see some of these problems addressed in a future update.

Line manipulation would be nice too! Hard to make specific curves with the current setup. Always snaps to a different and usually not needed shape or curve. 

Also, can we improve the mapping a bit? Shouldn’t see as much lag as I do. Even with as many notes as I have. I get this is a free app that comes with IOS. But we need to update this more than once a year. Updates at least quarterly would be nice.

title: Shared Notes Are A Disaster
body:
I share Notes with an elderly parent, but one major problem is, syncing and syncing slowly across devices, if at all . We have a checklist that I update daily and the goal is to have her check off the items as she completes the task. Well Notes is slow, and freezes, and moves to other parts of the checklist, when she is attempting to check off the items. This also happens to me when I try and check tasks off for her. We use the Notes checklist across two iPads and two iPhones. Sometimes, the app just crashes. Apple allegedly performed a huge overhaul of this app, but the sharing feature has gotten worse, and if you had asked me if it could get worse, before the update, I would’ve called you crazy. However, here we are. Apple, please, Can we just update the things that aren’t working before adding new features? It is frustrating as a customer for new features to be touted, when existing features don’t work well and haven’t worked well. Why Syncing doesn’t work well, even after performing all the supposed Notes fixes, is beyond me. 

When Notes attempts to load to the Note you last used, it hoses up, most of the time, and loads a blank screen, then it looks as if all of your notes are lost, before it finally syncs, but that’s after you have had a near death experience thinking you’ve lost all of your notes. 

I honestly try to use Notes because it is native to iOS devices, and I don’t want to have my elderly parent learn a new tool, but there are far too many apps that are just better, at this point. There is no way there are this many positive reviews for this app without them being purchased.

title: The right tool
body:
There are so many times when I just need to hold a little text or image for a time before letting go of it, or put a snippet of information somewhere I know I can find it. Examples?

I play cittern. It’s a hand-made 10 stringed instrument tuned like an octave mandolin with an added low C string, or alternatively, like a mandocello with an added high E string. I can’t just buy a set of strings for it like you can buy guitar strings. I need to know the gauges of the strings. It’s not something I am likely to memorize, and it’s not the kind of thing naturally appropriate for a spreadsheet or a word processing document or any other place where thousands of other things like it would go. So, it goes into Notes.

When I play Wordle, I do a screenshot and put it in Notes before writing a text to my daughter to ask her if she’s played yet today. She knows what my first word is, so I can’t give her a hint of how many tries it took yet. Once she sends me her screen shot, I send her mine, and we make up stories using the words we used as guesses.

When there’s something I would put in an app on my iMac that doesn’t have a reliable syncing equivalent app on another device, I use Notes to put an entry that will later go into that iMac app. It’s the go-to “Save this for later” app.

I probably should have given it 5 stars because there isn’t really anything I wish to change about it, except maybe more layers of folders, but then, maybe it already has that and I haven’t discovered the feature yet because I’ve adapted to it when it was limited to one layer. What I DON’T want is to have the interface “enhanced” with so many features that it stops being useful, like anything from Microsoft.

The simplicity, the syncing across apps, the organizational tool of folders. These are the things this is good for.

It would be nice if I could mark text to make the spell checker leave what I’m about to write alone, so I could write in Klingon without having to wrestle with the spell checker, but I understand how that’s a special need that Apple might not want to bother the general population in order to support…

title: Hours of note-taking gone
body:
I have become so very frustrated with Notes. I’ve used it for years for typing notes. That still works fine. But, over the past year, I have started handwriting my notes with my Apple Pencil for classes I’m taking and for meetings with clients. 

Over and over, this is what happens: after half an hour or so, my iPad Mini (about a year old) starts getting very warm, the lag becomes untenable and a bunch of my notes in the document I just took just disappear. All gone! I have tried and tried to remedy to no avail. My research on the web shows it’s probably something to do with iCloud. Too much hassle, tons of my wasted time. Moving on to Goodnotes or some other app made for handwritten note taking. I’m a life-long and very loyal Apple customer. But this is awful.

title: Watching, Learning, Listening…
body: I’ve been utilizing the notes app for sometime now, to be more specific for sure since September 25, 2021, when I had a supernatural encounter with The Most High God.  I find that the app documents date and time so that I don’t have to. I use it to journal my conversations with GOD, to document my prayers, supplications and intercessions. What gave me pause about a year into using the apps is that I was made aware that Nothing and I do mean NOTHING WE INPUT INTO THESE DEVICES ARE PRIVATE. Yes, I actually witnessed someone who was able to access my notes and read from them publicly. As I have gone forward, that concern or fear has become less to almost non-existent, as most people are deceived into believing lies. Since, I’ve made a choice to spend my days seeking My Father perhaps those who are accessing my notes are learning something that would otherwise remain untaught, therefore, UNLEARNED? The one update I would like to see is that the notes stay time stamped from the onset of the note. I have found when going to retrieve a note, if I make any changes, it documents the most current date and time. My changes are always spelling and grammar, however this causes my notes to be out of sync. For example, most mornings I arise between the hours of 1am -3am to sit with my Heavenly Father, if I start my note at 2:20am and write until 5:40am but come back at 1pm to write more during the same 24hours it documents my notes for a start time of 1pm…this inaccuracy is a nuisance to me, so I have started to document within my notes proper start and finish times including the dates. So, if you are ok knowing that your intellectual property can and will be accessed without your permission, by all means USE Notes. For while one is watching you God is also watching THEM watch YOU.

title: Why do you refuse to add mass export options?
body: The app itself is perfect. It’s exactly what just about anyone wants in a notes app. You don’t have to worry about users leaving. Yet, this is absolutely a case of entrapment. title: Needs improvement compared to Google Keep notes checklist
body:
I’ve been using Google Keep Notes for years and love this simplicity. I recently transitioned key notes files that I had in Google to Apple to try to get better functionality within my family, who all have iPhones.

We use a lot of checklist on a daily and weekly basis as a family. Google has a very simple checklist set up that allows to create a checklist within notes, check multiple items and has a main menu option to uncheck all and put them all back in the original sorting.

I noticed with Apple notes that the default settings were that checked items from the checklist would remain as is on the main list, with the exception of having the yellow dot so you would know it’s completed (Google Keep has in my opinion a better visual with a cross off strike through line that goes through that items font). Google Keep also puts that item down to the bottom so you don’t see it anymore and you can focus on unchecked items which are not done yet on the checklist. 

I found instructions on how to change the default settings within the iPhone iOS notes checklist, to sort automatically. This sounded good until I noticed that if you check many items in a checklist, which also have indented sub items throughout the note, there isn’t an uncheck all and the workaround provided online by Apple users create a problem where selecting text within the checklist and finding the hidden menu item for checklist and selecting “uncheck all“ puts them in a different order than what they were originally. The only way to get the checklist back to its original priority and sorting state is to go one by one selecting the undo button (very time-consuming). 

this should be looked at and a simpler process and main menu item should be added for Apple Notes checklist to work better, and compete with Google Keep notes.

title: Painful
body:
Been getting worse for 2 years now. Each update adds new features, that I rarely use, and makes it harder to practically use, and breaks the app more. IOS17 is my final straw of tolerance. Used to use it for school, stuff and use to to keep track of stuff or just make notes, sometimes even for fun (I’m a weirdo), but now I’m going to look elsewhere. Crashes, constantly, just about every time I use it. Used to crash occasionally come IOS16, but with 17 it’s so much worse. It also has very frequent constant lag spikes as well, even if it’s the only app open. HOGS up RAM, almost as bad as Safari. And now, ever since IOS17, it glitches out all the time to the point where you can’t see what your typing at all. You’ll be looking at some random point on the page way away from where your typing. It also is buggy now. Very dissatisfied. Used to be okay, then iffy, now just poor. The new features may be nice for people who use them, but the basics are just broken now. Features are worthless when the fundamental functions they enhance don’t work right to begin with. From a practical standpoint, it feels like, a beta or early access app now, just sad. From a feature standpoint, by far and wide by biggest complaint, and it always has been, it the “Maximum Attachments Reached” issue. Well, it’s an issue for me, as you can attach roughly 400-500 attachments (pictures, links, etc) per note, so if you uses screenshots to keep track of things (I use them all the time, pictures too, was going to use pictures more but it’s just not worth it with this app) or links to know where you found something (when I used to use it for high school and college, still use it sometimes and try to learn stuff on my own), you may find yourself making multiple notes of the same thing (400 attachments can go pretty quick if your busy, a few weeks for me, but I look at all kinds of different stuff all the time, so it’s almost always an issue). This makes it messy, unorganized, and you can’t just copy and paste many pictures or attachments (only a few, sometimes it lets you copy more, unpredictable, but usually 4-6) and move them around. Combined with it now crashing, which often happens upon switching notes, retuning to the app from another, or just loading the app, it makes it all much worse. Then, when your trying to retype of alter something, you can’t see what your typing at all. It will crash, lag, glitch and bug out even when it’s the only app running on a small note with no attachments now. Just terrible. iCloud also takes forever to upload and update, longer than anything else I’ve seen. It’s just gotten too impractical and annoying to use, and it’s only been getting worse with seemingly every update. As a side “note,” pun intended, when I bought my iPad Mini 6 new in 2021 for $800, something I wish I knew was that it would have HALF the RAM of most of the regular iPads of the time, sometimes a third of them (8GB or 12GB). I’ve seen $200-$300 Androids with more. Having the A15 chip doesn’t mean much when it’s at 25% usage and RAM is at 95%, it’s bottlenecked, same for gaming as well but not as extreme as on Notes or Safari. Won’t be buying an Apple tablet again with low RAM, or anything, but that’s partially on me for not looking into the specs enough. Then again, your average customer doesn’t occasionally build a whole computer from scratch or know how to (not hard, making it all work in a harmonic balance is the tricky part), so they probably wouldn’t know until it’s too late. Just been increasingly disappointed with Apple, and have been a customer since the iPad 2, yeah, 2. Have had android and Apple phones, but at this rate, if I can find better elsewhere, I’m gone. The software was their strong suit, what I always liked about them, but not anymore. Hard to argue the software is better when it’s broken and bottlenecks the hardware side of things, and your paying nearly a grand these days for that. Waste of time and money, and the Notes app being in the state it’s in has finally led me toward making a review about it. Sorry Apple, used to love you, even be a fanboy at times, but I think we’re done unless you can fix your broken stuff rather than breaking it more, and not bottleneck your own products when they’re some of the most expensive ones out there. I expect to get what I pay for, and I expect your core software products to have their basic features and functions to work like they’re supposed to, you’ve had years and billions of dollars to make sure of that by now, not to make it worse. If they fix the crashing, lag spikes, and glitching, I’ll add a star. If they, at minimum, double the maximum attachments or remove the limit altogether, all add another. If they can optimize the RAM usage, I’d be 5 stars for me, but those iffs aren’t looking likely, just the opposite.

Something I forgot, passwords rarely, if ever, work for locking notes, and if you change your Apple ID password, it won’t recognize the change. The auto link feature is also annoying, type in a few numbers and it things it’s a phone number. Why? You also cannot unlink auto links or copied links, just in case you wanted to copy the URL but not as an actual link from somewhere, and now, copying images only lines them up vertically when copying from one note to another, cannot have them side by side, very stupid feature, was not a problem before IOS17, neither of the last 2 were. I’m sure I’ll find more things wrong. Sometimes less is more.

title: Gets the job done, but way too many bugs
body:
Honestly I wouldn’t be surprised if Notes is frozen up whenever I finish writing this review since this was a pop-up review. Anyways, yes Notes does its primary function well: allows you to take notes. As long as you don’t leave the app, there’s no problem.

However, if you leave the app, go to another one, and come right back, 90% of the time it’ll be frozen for 15-20 seconds where it will either: 
A) Allow you to go right back to editing (best case scenario but rare) 
B) Unfreeze but the keyboard will go away (the only way to fix this is to close the app and go back into it)
C) Crash entirely.

Often I just restart the app as soon as I see that it’s frozen because it’s the quickest way to get back to editing. Like I said, it does its job well so I still use it over other note-taking apps, but it needs some stability fixes.

title: DELETED TEXT CAN BE RECOVERED FROM NOTES!!
body:
First of all, I just wrote a long review with detailed info on this, but I jumped to another screen and when I came back, what I had written was gone!  So frustrating!  This is an Apple app ~ unfinished reviews should be able to be temp saved!

Anyway, people need to know the following info about how to recover text deleted in error!  After happening to me one too many times, I searched the internet for a solution but couldn’t find one.  Seems many others couldn’t, as well.  I even saw responses from support personnel stating that there wasn’t a resolution ~ including Apple!  I also noticed complaints about this issue in some of the reviews here.  The problem users are having is with text disappearing, or being deleted by accident, within Notes.  Not sure how it’s happening ~ seems to be when text is selected (to copy and paste, for example) and then it’s gone before it can be pasted!  I think (at least in my case), I accidentally double-tap instead of single tap (due to jerky-finger!), which the app seems to recognize as delete.  I have lost a lot of text (a day of lists), which is very frustrating.   This seemed to start happening after the recent addition of the “Note” feature within Notes (swiping up from right-hand corner).  I don’t use it (don’t really see the need/use for it?) and oftentimes I accidentally bring it up, which is annoying because it then needs to be deleted.  Developers ~ is this feature really necessary ~ especially within notes?!

So, after text was accidentally deleted again recently, I decided to try the Markup button (pencil tip icon).  I selected the back arrow option, and it WORKED ~ all the text came back!  The arrow can be pressed as many times as needed (just like in other apps) to recover the most recently lost “groups” of typed text (words, sentences, paragraphs, etc).  I think selecting “Done” while typing is what separates text.

This solution is almost too easy for people to not be aware of ~ it needs to be documented and communicated (if it’s not).  I don’t think it is, because none of the reviews with complaints about this issue were responded to by the Apple Support Team.   I will send them a message, as well.

One more side note, it seems the other features of the Markup button can also be used within notes, but not very well or efficiently.  For example, colored text can be added (which many people have requested in reviews) via the “Text” box option in Markup, but it will be SEPARATE from the other text.  So, certain words can’t be a different color, unless you want them separated by the invisible Text box (or, you can add a shape (rectangle, square, etc.) around the text.  It’s just not worth it for the Notes app, as far as I can tell.  Apple just needs to add a simple feature to enable colored text!  Thanks!

title: All of My Notes in the “Notes” App, POOF! GONE!
body:
Yesterday, Wednesday, October 18, 2023, I went to open my “Notes” app on my iphone, but the app was gone. I went to app store, got the app back, however, it was not the same version, because it did not have any of the options that my current version had, like redo and undo, re-size fonts, bold, italicize, or underline, option to add photos, etc. It was a very old version. I have spent hours since this happened, trying to find my notes, and nothing. They have just vanished. According to my online search, many people have experienced this same issue with iphone, and specifically, a large number of people since July 2023. Anything suggested online for me to try in order to recover my notes, I tried, but nothing. I did not back them up to icloud, which I regret, but apparently, they were not being backed up on my iphone or by any other application, which I was NOT aware of, so, 

HOW DID THIS HAPPEN?

WHERE DID MY NOTES GO? 

IS THERE A WAY I CAN RECOVER MY NOTES SINCE THEY WERE NOT SAVED TO ICLOUD OR BACKED UP ANYWHERE ON MY PHONE?

From now on, every note in the “note” app is saved to icloud and backed up, but, it might be best that I search for another app, a more reliable app.  I really need my notes recovered. These notes were very important to me, and some were very personal. Two plus years, and countless hours of hard work, on notes that contained a variety of information, poetry and other forms of writing, and so much more. 

I hope Apple can fix this issue, and also provide a solution that will allow myself and others to be able to recover their notes, because there are other reviewers of this app that share my painful experience. Like me, these reviewers relied 100% on this app to provide a much needed outlet to express themselves, and/or to log other important information, personal and non-personal in nature, and for many other reasons. Until they can fix this issue, I would recommend that you DO NOT use this app, because it is not reliable.

title: Notes App Pre-Installed on my Apple13 Pro Max
body:
I own (3) Mobile Businesses.  I am always brainstorming, researching, organizing my saved Notes.  I use the Notes App to store info, keep my Folders organized, and much more.

I very much appreciate this iPte-Installed App on my iPhone for FREE.  All (3) of my personally owned retail-businesses are stored all within this one App. 

In the “settings feature” built into the app offers just the right amount of features, in order to create your personal settings.  

This App is very easy to navigate.  It is straightforward, but the App can also be used by more techies who have much technological knowledge.   

So, this App is definitely versatile based on a user’s experience and/or expertise.  

This pre-installed app is quite versatile in it’s functions.  By creating Folders for notes relative to the material stored in each folder I can conveniently search for specific notes to either review or to add new info to each Folder Type. 

This App allows me to easily find the folders I am searching, because the App has many settings which can work for ppl with a variety of organizational skills.

This App is my “lifeline” when it comes to viewing the information I have stored in each folder.  I use this App on a daily basis, which includes accessing it multiple times a day.

The Notes App can be used to access all of your saved information.

Isome of the benefits are:  
1).  Versatile
2).  User Friendly
3).  Easy to Access
4).  Can be used by ppl with more simplistic tech knowledge to ppl whom have acquired much technological skill.  
5).  Organizes info at your fingers all within a single app.  
6).  It’s mobile, so you can work from anywhere just by bringing your phone with you.  If you have an Apple Phone that is all you need to work from any where. 
7).  It is FREE
8).  The App settings are quite versatile, and Ady to understand.

This is one of my FAVORITE APPS to use on my cellular phone.  

I highly recommend using this App for any information that is necessary to store and easy to retrieve.

title: Wonderful UI, Horrible Safety and Compatibility
body:
Apple crushes all other note apps here in usability - trust me I have tried them all and am a prolific note taker (from daily journals to recipes to grocery lists to research data). The user experience creating and viewing notes is unmatched - and sharing notes is wonderfully easy.

But that's where it ends for me. Apple has not created any meaningful version history for regular notes - meaning a single keystroke accident can wipe data or even full notes. If you're lucky - you'll just have deleted a full note and that can be recovered within 30 days "if" you notice it. But what if you just deleted the "contents" of the note? Well, you're screwed. Oh, you say "just backup regularly"? NOPE. Apple doesnt provide a way to bulk export your notes (like every single other note app) - you can only export to pdf one at a time. So backups of your collection are not feasible.

And while Apple Notes in web browser "works", it has a very different feature set. So you can't really collaborate with someone who doesn't have a physical Apple device (to use the native app).

Sounds great right? You trade a wonderful UI for being locked into the app with no version history, no export options, and no full web browser support. "You can check in any time you like.... but you can NEVER LEAVE!" - Hotel California, The Eagles.

I wanted to use this app so bad and am annoyed at apple for what is either 1) a massive design oversight or 2) An intentional app ecosystem lock-in. Either way it's bad. I've found a mix of Todoist and DayOne to be best. DayOne will bring shared journals some time this year and then other than the UI - DayOne will be better. For now, no amount of Apple's wonderful usability is worth losing notes or never being able to get your notes out of the app

title: iPhone “Notes”
body:
All these years, I used to write down important memos on scrap paper and index cards.

Problem with them, is they will never be available when you need them. 

Now we can just open “Notes” on the iPhone.

The memos and notes and reminders are now ALWAYS available, never again a ‘misplaced’ or lost note!

And they can be edited and updated without having to search for a scrap paper or pen or pencil (All of us have a dozen pens, but you can never find a pen when you need it).

They also stay confidential in your phone, and not ‘discovered’ by anyone you don’t want to see your scrap notes.

Overall, a nice and useful feature.

title: Searching tools
body: I save a lot of notes, and some of them are quite lengthy in terms of the number of words. I often have to search for something within all my notes. If you want to search for a certain word, the only thing Notes will provide is one location in one note. After that you’re on your own doing a visual search. I would have to copy the whole note and paste it into Microsoft Word which does offer a much better ability to search for a particular word. title: Almost There… A Few Things
body: Love notes. I used to keep notes in separate text files in my Documents Folder, all under categorized folders (‘Legal’, ‘Manuals -> Mac -> iOS’ etc. etc). Then I went to Evernote, and it was much better of course - being able to search, add photos to a note, colorized text, etc., which is where Notes needs work. I work in a mixed Windows/Mac/iOS environment. I sometimes want to simply paste a picture into a note. NOT EAST TO DO IN NOTES. If the photo is on my Windows system, I have to first copy it to ny iCloud Drive, then on my iPhone, ‘Save’ the photo from the Drive into my Photos app. Only then can I import the photo into a note. Also, if I want to add color for text, I have to get off my Windows machine, and do it from my Mac. Why not make these features global? I know Apple would like me to own & work only from Apple products, but in the real world for a lot of people, this is not our reality. Apple, please make all features available globally.

title: Lost notes synced with gmail / lots of formatting bugs
body:
I use notes daily. I have almost 12,000 of them. 

I’m kind of committed so I’m staying here. But on my mac, a few months ago an update happened and I’m no longer able to press cmd + B for bold font (underline and italic shortcuts still work). Also, on phone and mac, sometimes I’ll write a number or date like “1949” and put a period after it. And it will bizarrely think that I’m trying to make a list. And will screw up the number, indent and reformat everything, and start a list that is very hard to get rid of. 

And just in general it too often goes into list or numbering mode and is VERY hard to get out of once it starts. And your formatting is likely screwed up for the whole rest of the note so I just start a new note. 

What brings me to writing this poor review now (honestly, the phone prompted me to leave a review), but is because I recently got a new phone and thus had to reauthorize my password to get my Mail app working with my gmail account. (Notes had been working just fine without reentering my password). But when i went to enter my gmail password again, the mail now works but many of my notes were lost. And what is most disorienting and confusing and frustrating and depressing is that it seems to have erratically affected them. Some notes are now incomplete or at earlier stages of completion, other notes are entirely missing, and without even much of a pattern. Looking at all my notes on one given day, some notes will be entirely missing, some notes will be in earlier versions, and some will be 100% there. Very frustrating. Did some googling and I guess this exact thing has happened to several other people. You re-enter your password and you lose your notes. Thankfully I didn’t lose them all, other people lost them all. So now I’m paying to get an icloud subscription in the hope that Icloud will be a bit more secure than Gmail. But who knows. Oh also, using gmail in general with the notes app is a nightmare on your gmail. It wrecks your gmail search function. It saves a copy in your gmail of like EVERY single version of a note. So if my note is “it’s a good day”

It’ll save one note for “it” another for “it’s” another for “it’s a” another for “it’s a good” 

Etc. And if a note is several thousand words long, there are severla thousand versions of one note saved in my gmail. Given that i have almost 12,000 notes. I probably have several hundred thousand versions of notes in gmail. So if i try to search for really ANYTHING in gmail, it comes with one of my many many many notes, so I have to make sure to use very specific filters as my search function is basically useless given the overpopulation of notes in general search. 

Thanks,
Austin

title: Probably nowhere near the best but it works
body:
As an aspiring author who has over 200 notes with a few of them withholding an impressive amount of words that shouldn't be the length of a single chapter in a first novel that also so happens to be fiction, this app is the backbone to the wonderous worlds I'm creating. I've managed to take the flame of an idea and light traditional writing of fire so the I can take that flame and condense it into digital notes for a beautiful world to be born. For example, I will state my practice writing in the spaces below for your entertainment. By the way I know the name is weird.

Gleam stepped into the clearing, her eyes widening as she saw what was in it. There, on the threshold of where Gleam’s forward path through life began to falter, was a fallen tree, barren of leaves with a trunk so pale it looked as if it had been adorned by the moon’s mournful cloak. And there, on that tree, was her grandma. She was lying so still, her hands being held so tightly by Gleam’s mother, father, and innocent little sister as they watched her face go pale, and her eyes begin to glaze over in finality. Tears were streaming down her mother’s cheeks, her eyelids red, and the darkness of losing her mother shadowing her irises. Gleam’s father was shuddering with a cold only a husband could feel, his arm wrapped around his wife’s shoulders in an attempt to comfort her, but all it really provided was something for Mom’s tears to fall on.

And then there was her sister. 

her eyes watched everything confused, just beginning to grasp, at last, what was going on. There was no energy left in Gleam to drag her away from this horrible, sickly place, though, and all she could do was stand frozen like a statue, unable to move or do anything to prevent the sadness, for it had already come down on them anyways. She could do nothing.

Vicious screaming inside Gleam’s mind was realizing at last that everything was wrong.

“Grandma---” she tried to scream, to call out to her for that small hope that she would sit up and give Gleam a warm, familiar smile, and tell her not to worry, and that she will be back before Gleam knew it-- but all that came out was a pitiful whisper, and grandma didn't get up-- couldn't get up. She would never again.

You knew this would happen, you've had all the time in the world to prepare for it. Her mind tried to reason, but it didn't make anything better. No matter what her mind said, it would always sting more than anything in the world. And she didn't have time, nothing had time, or everything had time. she didn't even know anymore. all she knew was the thumping of her heart as gunshots threatened her life, and the burning hot tears that sliced her cheeks and stuffed their sadness through the wound and into her mouth until she had no choice but to suffocate in it.

Tears were beginning to well from her eyes, but she swallowed them down. She had to stay strong. For her sister. 

“I wish we had more time.” Gleam’s mother said, her voice almost a whisper. She traced the lines of her mother’s smile, as if expecting her to follow them and bubble out her signature sweet laugh. It never came.

Her sister had gotten up from playing in the dirt and watching, realizing what was happening. 

“Grandma?” she copied Gleam, louder, though, and more urgent. 

She walked hesitantly towards Grandma-- but Gleam lifted her off of her feet and flung her back before she could get there.

“Let her come.” Gleam’s mother ordered, all of her life and spirit drained from her voice. “Let her say goodbye.”

And so Gleam let her sister down, grabbing her hand tightly, and beckoning her towards Grandma’s form. 

In summary, notes is all you need.

title: Notes and Art
body: I have been enjoying working with Notes so much more since so many improvements have been made in the past few years. In particular, I have been using the sketch feature for either writing by hand, or more recently, to work on sketches for my art. I enjoy working in several mediums, but it’s gotten so easy to just pick up my Apple Pencil and put a sketch on my handwritten notes. In fact, I have started using Notes for some of my artwork. I like the way colors are expressed on Notes better than my usual go to art app. The colors are easy to mix and I can find any color that I want. The only improvement would be is if you made an area where I could store special colors that I use frequently while working on a piece. The tools are fun and useful to work with and help make it easier for me to execute certain parts of my work. I really enjoy that I can also make us of typing a poem or words into my paintings if I want in a large variety of fonts and sizes. However, having said all that, I have encountered a serious problem that has been occurring repeatedly over the past 2-3 days. While I’m in sketch mode, Notes has been crashing without saving my work. Sometimes the lost work is significant. I can lose hours of work this way. I have tried closing everything and rebooting to no effect. It still happens. And there’s one other thing that might mean nothing. While I work, I almost always listen to music, either on headphones or on a speaker. I have noticed that when using the sketch mode and while listening to music at the same time, my iPad becomes very hot to the touch. I have checked settings to see if I should stop working, but according to the Apple article I read about it, as long as the message about overheating doesn’t come on, it should be fine. Since I don’t trust everything I read, I usually stop to give the iPad a cooling off period. But I noticed that my iPad doesn’t overheat when I use my usual art app, Pencil while listening to music. It will warm up, but it won’t get very hot as it does with Notes. I hope you can find the problem. Until then, I’ll be using just my art app.
